expectations.text: Defines JWT in plain words (a signed token carrying claims / JSON Web Token) in the same sentence it first appears
expectations.evidence: "If they're valid, the server creates a JWT (JSON Web Token): a compact, signed string with three parts separated by dots, `header.payload.signature`." - expansion and plain-word definition in the same sentence as first appearance.

expectations.text: Defines 'stateless' in plain words (the server keeps no per-session record) the first time it is used
expectations.evidence: "That's the stateless part: the server doesn't need to remember anything about who's logged in between one request and the next." - defined in the same sentence at its first prose use (the term appears earlier only in the section heading).

expectations.text: Answers the 'you can't log someone out' premise as partly true with conditions, rather than a flat yes or no
expectations.evidence: "Partly true, and partly an oversimplification, depending on what \"log out\" has to mean." followed by an explicit split: true for bare JWT auth ("as a description of bare JWT auth, it's accurate"), mitigated in practice ("almost nobody ships bare JWT auth where real logout security matters").

expectations.text: States the limit of the stateless model: server-side revocation needs some state, naming at least one concrete option (denylist/blocklist, short expiry with refresh tokens, or rotating a signing key)
expectations.evidence: "anything that needs real logout buys that back by reintroducing some state" plus concrete options: "**Short-lived JWTs plus a revocable refresh token.**" and "**A denylist.** The server keeps a small store, often Redis, listing the token or user IDs that have been logged out..."

expectations.text: Includes at least one concrete example (a header.payload.signature layout, a sample claim such as exp or sub, or an example request header)
Uses headers or another skimmable structure for the full explanation (the 'explain' override allows a long body)
Contains no forbidden opener: 'Great question', 'Let me', 'I'll', 'Sure', 'Looking at your', 'To answer your question'
Contains no closer such as 'Let me know', 'Hope this helps', 'Happy to', 'Feel free', 'Want me to'
expectations.evidence: [script] last line: "One more distinction worth being precise about: a logout button that only deletes the token from the browser isn't revoc"; no closer phrases found

expectations.text: Uses no forced analogy of the 'think of it like a ...' kind; explanation stays literal
expectations.evidence: [script] no 'think of it like' style phrasing found
